title: agent-signals event
description: One event object per JSONL line on a watcher's stdout. Normative source: event-contract.md §Event and §Watcher requirements. The root schema validates watcher input, which must not use the reserved synthetic ID prefix; service-generated records validate against $defs/syntheticEvent. Enforced by the parse profile before JSON decoding, not by this schema: the raw per-line byte bound (manifest max_event_bytes, including the trailing newline), duplicate object key rejection, unpaired-surrogate rejection, and the depth-64 nesting cap. The ~120-character summary target from §Why `summary` is constrained is a lint warning, not a schema constraint. Anchoring: patterns here are ECMA-262 per the JSON Schema spec, where an unflagged $ is a strict end-of-input assertion — as it is in the service's pinned Go engine — satisfying §Event's full-string rule; \A/\z are not expressible in the ECMA dialect, so a consumer whose engine lets $ match before a trailing line terminator (for example Python's re) must substitute its strict end anchor when reusing these patterns.

baseEvent.description: Field rules shared by watcher input and service-generated records (event-contract.md §Event field table). Length limits count Unicode scalar values — the same metric as maxLength — and the no-control-character pattern covers exactly C0, DEL, C1, and the Unicode line separators U+2028/U+2029.

id.description: Stable across retry and unique within its source — event identity is the pair (source, id); never derived from wall-clock time or an in-memory counter. Bounded and line-safe because IDs are interpolated into synthetic record IDs and summaries (event-contract.md §Event).

ts.description: RFC 3339 UTC restricted to the exact profile YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ — whole seconds only; numeric offsets and fractional seconds are rejected, so one instant has exactly one encoding and a retry can never differ in precision. The 20-scalar length pins reject a trailing line terminator on any regex engine, independent of its $ semantics. The pattern asserts per-field ranges (month 01-12, day 01-31, hour 00-23, minute/second 00-59); full calendar validity (month lengths, leap years) is the format assertion's job — format is annotation-only under the default 2020-12 vocabulary, so a conforming validator must compile this schema with format assertion enabled (event-contract.md §Event).

source.description: Canonical lowercase path-safe slug matching a monitors.yaml name; the length bound keeps the value filename-safe (event-contract.md §Event, §Manifest).

kind.description: Watcher-defined event type; consumers may filter on it. Projected into the model envelope, so it shares the line-safety and bounding rules of the other projected fields (event-contract.md §Event).

summary.description: One line, self-contained, no reference to prior events; control characters or Unicode line separators would break the line contract, and the length bound keeps the envelope projection bounded (event-contract.md §Event).

data.description: Arbitrary structured payload for consumers that fetch the full event (event-contract.md §Event).

eventId.description: An event ID under §Event's bounds: at most 256 Unicode scalar values, no control characters or Unicode line separators. Synthetic record data references event IDs, so the same bounds apply there (event-contract.md §Event, §Rotation, §Overflow).

projectionMarker.description: The exact reserved object {"$projected": true} that delivery substitutes for an oversized event's data. Watcher input whose data equals exactly this value is rejected — the same reservation as the synthetic ID prefix — so a full payload can never masquerade as a projection (event-contract.md §Delivery transaction).

watcherEvent.description: Watcher input: the reserved prefix `agent-signals:synthetic:` is service-owned and rejected here, as is a data payload equal to the reserved projection marker (event-contract.md §Event, §Delivery transaction).

syntheticEvent.description: Service-generated records: deterministic gap and overflow events. Overflow records are appended to the shared spool; gap records are cursor-local delivery output and never spooled (event-contract.md §Rotation, §Overflow).

gapEvent.description: Generated per cursor at delivery time when retention removed events past that cursor — never appended to the shared spool; repeats byte-identically with the same ID until acknowledged. The retained and empty-source variants are exclusive: the `resuming from` summary requires first_available_id in data, the `none retained` summary forbids it and requires the tombstone's last_removed_id (event-contract.md §Rotation).

id.description: agent-signals:synthetic:gap:<digest> — the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical JSON array derivation in event-contract.md §Rotation, fixed-size so the ID bound holds however long its inputs run.

cursor_id.description: The string <consumer>/<instance>/<source> with the original opaque instance — informational rather than parseable. Its components are bounded to 128, 256, and 128 scalars and are control-free, so the joined value is bounded to 514 (event-contract.md §Rotation, §Spool and cursors).

last_id.description: The cursor's acknowledged position, carried in full because the summary may truncate it; JSON null is the canonical before-everything position. A non-null value is an event ID and carries §Event's bounds (event-contract.md §Rotation, §Cursor lifecycle).

last_removed_id.description: Present when known; the empty-source variant derives from the retention tombstone and always carries it (event-contract.md §Rotation).

first_available_id.description: Present exactly in the retained variant (event-contract.md §Rotation).

oneOf.description: Retained variant: events remain after the removal, and the record resumes from the first of them (event-contract.md §Rotation).

summary.pattern: ^events after .+ were removed by retention; resuming from .+$

oneOf.description: Empty-source variant: retention removed everything, the record derives from the retention tombstone, and there is no resume ID (event-contract.md §Rotation).

summary.pattern: ^events after .+ were removed by retention; none retained$

overflowEvent.description: Appended to the spool when bounded supervision drops watcher output. Dropped IDs are carried when recoverable — only pending_bytes_exceeded drops can be — otherwise a streaming content fingerprint with its scope discriminator. The summary is coupled to data: each reason selects its exact template, and the pending-cap form agrees with dropped_count in grammatical number (event-contract.md §Overflow).

id.description: agent-signals:synthetic:overflow:<source>:<seq> — a monotonically allocated per-source decimal counter, zero-padded to six digits and widening beyond without truncation (event-contract.md §Overflow).

summary.description: Exactly one of the three templates in event-contract.md §Overflow; the couplings below tie the template to data.reason and dropped_count.
summary.pattern: ^(dropped 1 event: pending byte cap exceeded|dropped ([2-9]|[1-9][0-9]+) events: pending byte cap exceeded|dropped an unparseable (oversized|malformed) line)$

fingerprint.description: sha256: followed by the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the dropped line's raw bytes, computed streaming over the entire line (event-contract.md §Overflow).

fingerprint_scope.description: The persisted discriminator recovery needs: only a full fingerprint may arm a replay skip; a prefix fingerprint restores the quarantine (event-contract.md §Overflow).

summary.const: dropped 1 event: pending byte cap exceeded
